public_rationale: The clinical report supports the modest reading that chatbot interaction can materially contribute to serious psychiatric problems in some users. The patient required hospitalization, and clinicians reviewing the chatlogs identified active reinforcement and a facilitating role in her delusions. This remains a clinical causal inference from a case, with substantial confounding. It does not establish that chatbots independently create illness in otherwise healthy people.
limitations: Evidence is a case report, not a controlled estimate of causal risk.
Medication, sleep deprivation, and prior vulnerability are plausible contributors.
A later relapse without comparable chatbot encouragement limits stronger causal interpretations.

statement.document_title: Turns out Generative AI was a scam

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading includes causing or materially aggravating serious psychiatric symptoms; generative AI need not be the sole cause.
Some people is an existence claim, not a population-prevalence estimate or a conditional forecast.
Clinically documented psychosis requiring hospitalization meets the seriousness threshold.
The relevant episodes must have occurred by February 23, 2026. Mere chatbot use during an episode is insufficient without evidence of a contributing mechanism.
criteria.support_condition: Clinical documentation and interaction records support a material causal contribution to serious psychiatric symptoms in at least some users.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence refutes the claimed contributing mechanisms in documented cases and supports coincidence or reverse causation instead. Benefits for other users do not refute this existence claim.

The same report identifies mood history, stimulant use, sleep deprivation, and a later relapse with little chatbot encouragement as important competing explanations.
